entries.name: companion-identity-not-derived-from-the-source
entries.claim: The companion transaction and line identities are a pure function of the stock-count source record ids. Deriving them from anything else -- here, from fresh randomness -- means the kernel mints a companion identity nothing can recompute, which is exactly the `#companionDerivation` copies-rather-than-derives defect `purchasing-sales-v1-plan.md` section 7.16 measured. Scope of this entry's evidence: the kill set is measured within the three `companion derivation` tests this command runs, which is what the runner observes; the mutation also reds the wider stock-count file, and that is stated rather than measured here.

kills.name: stock-count companion derivation: a source with no pre-staged transaction posts and the kernel writes both companion identities
kills.expected: does not carry the derived companion transaction identity

kills.name: stock-count companion derivation: the companion transaction and its lines are the kernel projection of the count
kills.expected: does not carry the derived companion transaction identity

entries.name: companion-revision-left-at-the-column-default
entries.claim: The kernel WRITES the companion transaction's revision, derived as sourceRevision + 1, rather than letting the column default supply it. Both companions of one posting carry the same derived revision, so a reader can join a posted count to its companion and see one consistent pair; a companion left at the default disagrees with the source it projects.

kills.expected: does not carry the derived companion transaction identity

entries.name: source-companion-column-never-written
entries.claim: The posted transition is where the source's companion transaction identity is written. Writing null there instead of the derived identity leaves a posted stock count whose companion column is still empty -- the source posts, the movements land, and nothing records which transaction they belong to. That is the silent-until-reconciled failure this packet's Band A declaration is about. The mutation writes `NULLIF($11, $11)` rather than deleting the assignment, because deleting it leaves the bound parameter unreferenced and PostgreSQL then refuses the statement with 42P18 -- a red, but not this red, and an entry whose kill dies for the wrong reason certifies nothing.

kills.name: stock-count companion derivation: a source with no pre-staged transaction posts and the kernel writes both companion identities
kills.expected: does not carry the derived companion transaction identity

kills.name: stock-count companion derivation: the companion transaction and its lines are the kernel projection of the count
kills.expected: does not carry the derived companion transaction identity

entries.name: source-line-companion-column-never-written
entries.claim: Line-level companion identity is written per source line, not implied by the header. Writing null instead still satisfies the update's own row count -- the guard is `IS NULL` and the row stays null -- so only the read-back catches it. This is the vacuity vector where a write reports success and the fact does not hold. `NULLIF($5, $5)` keeps the bound parameter referenced, for the reason recorded on `source-companion-column-never-written`.

kills.expected: lines do not all carry a derived companion line identity

kills.expected: lines do not all carry a derived companion line identity

entries.name: reviewed-source-companion-must-be-null-fence-removed
entries.claim: The kernel is the ONLY writer of a companion identity, so a reviewed stock count must not already name one. Replacing the fence with whatever is stored makes the kernel ADOPT a companion transaction written by something else. Measured, the posting is still refused -- the line check catches it further down -- so what the fence actually buys is the IDENTITY of the refusal: with it, the operator is told the reviewed session is wrong; without it, they are sent to a line that is fine. This is the packet's gate-invisible deliverable, and it dies alone: the two posting tests are unaffected because their stored value is null either way.
entries.original:
const expectedCompanionId =
    state === binding.stockCountReviewedState ? null : command.transactionId;

kills.name: stock-count companion derivation: a reviewed count that already names a companion transaction is refused
kills.expected: the refusal must name the reviewed session, not one of its lines

entries.name: family-roster-transaction-type-repointed
entries.claim: The companion transaction's type comes from the compiled family roster's ROLE binding, not from a switch arm, and each of the stock_count family's two roles carries its own. Repointing the `count` role's declared transaction type changes what the kernel writes for an initial count while leaving a correction alone -- which is what makes the roster load-bearing per role rather than decorative. It dies alone: only the projection test posts an initial count AND reads its companion's type.

kills.name: stock-count companion derivation: the companion transaction and its lines are the kernel projection of the count
kills.expected: the count role companion type comes from the family role binding

entries.name: companion-business-key-not-derived-from-identity
entries.claim: The companion transaction's business key is derived from the derived identity, so it is unique whenever the identity is. `inventory_transaction_number` is `tenantEnvironmentCaseInsensitiveUnique`, so a fixed number lets the FIRST companion in a tenant write and makes every later one impossible -- the projection test posts an opening count and then a correction, and the correction cannot get a companion at all. MEASURED, AND NOT WHAT WAS FIRST DECLARED: the collision surfaces as INVENTORY_POSTING_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT naming a natural effect race, because the savepoint's 23505 handler predates the kernel writing a companion and attributes every unique violation to a movement identity. The red is real and attributable to this mutation; the DIAGNOSIS the kernel prints is wrong, and that is filed as `companion-key-collision-misreported-as-effect-race` rather than repaired here.

kills.name: stock-count companion derivation: the companion transaction and its lines are the kernel projection of the count
kills.expected: a natural effect identity was claimed by a different posting

entries.name: companion-derivation-namespace-moved
entries.claim: Companion identity must be STABLE, not merely deterministic, because it is the join a reconciliation reader recomputes against already-posted counts. Moving the derivation namespace produces a derivation that is still pure and still deterministic, so write and read-back agree and the kernel's own `assertCompanionIdentitiesPersisted` passes -- it recomputes with the same function it wrote with. Only the golden vectors catch it, which is what makes them load-bearing rather than decorative. It dies alone: every other assertion in the packet compares the kernel against the same derivation and moves with it.

kills.name: stock-count companion derivation: a source with no pre-staged transaction posts and the kernel writes both companion identities
kills.expected: the companion transaction derivation must be stable across releases
